banks.title: Community Health Nursing, Primary Health Care, Epidemiology & Communicable Disease Control

questions.prompt: A barangay health worker asks the nurse to confirm which level of prevention an immunization campaign for healthy infants belongs to. Which response is correct?
options: A. Primary level - health promotion and illness prevention
B. Secondary level - early diagnosis and prompt treatment
C. Tertiary level - rehabilitation and disability limitation
D. Quaternary level - palliative pain management
questions.rationale: The material classifies primary level prevention as health education and immunization given while the patient is still healthy, aimed at health promotion and illness prevention; secondary is early detection/treatment and tertiary is rehabilitation/palliative care.

questions.prompt: A mother brings her 2-month-old for the first pentavalent dose. After administration, which instruction by the nurse is most appropriate regarding the expected side effect?
options: A. Give paracetamol round-the-clock every 6 hours for 24 hours for fever
B. Apply a warm compress to the injection site for local tenderness
C. Withhold the next dose permanently because fever always follows
D. Return immediately for any low-grade fever as it signals an emergency
questions.rationale: The source lists fever as a side effect of pentavalent managed with paracetamol round-the-clock every 6 hours for 24 hours, and local tenderness managed with a COLD compress (not warm); seizure within 3 days is the adverse effect that contraindicates further doses, not ordinary fever.

questions.prompt: During an immunization session, an infant vomits 10 minutes after receiving oral polio vaccine (OPV). What is the appropriate nursing action?
options: A. Repeat the dose because the infant vomited within 30 minutes
B. Do not repeat the dose since the vaccine is already absorbed
C. Withhold all further OPV doses for this child
D. Switch the route and give the dose intramuscularly
questions.rationale: The material states that if a child vomits OPV within 30 minutes the dose should be given again; if vomiting occurs after 30 minutes, it is not repeated.

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing cold chain requirements. Which vaccines are identified as MOST sensitive to heat and stored in the freezer (-15C to -25C)?
questions.rationale: The source identifies OPV and MMR (with Varicella) as most sensitive to heat, requiring freezer storage at -15C to -25C, whereas BCG, Hepa B, pentavalent, PCV, Rota, IPV and TT are kept in the body of the refrigerator at +2C to +8C.

questions.prompt: According to the Letter of Instruction 949, which is considered the MOST important of the four pillars of Primary Health Care?
questions.rationale: The material lists active community participation as the most important among the four pillars of PHC (the others being intra/intersectoral linkages, appropriate technology, and support mechanisms).

questions.prompt: A nurse computes vital statistics for a community. Which index is described as the BEST single indicator of the health status of the whole community?
questions.rationale: The source describes Swaroop's Index (total deaths of those over 50 divided by total deaths) as the measure of proportionate mortality and the best index of health status of the whole community.

questions.prompt: Using the Maglaya scoring for prioritizing family health problems, which criterion carries the highest weight (Wt: 2) and is described as the most important?
questions.rationale: In the Maglaya prioritization the material assigns Modifiability of the problem a weight of 2 and labels it the most important, while nature, preventive potential and salience each carry a weight of 1.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assigned to a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which transmission-based precaution is required?
options: A. Airborne precaution with an N95 mask in a negative-pressure room
B. Droplet precaution with a surgical mask within 1 meter
C. Contact precaution with gloves and gown only
D. Protective environment with positive pressure and HEPA filter
questions.rationale: The material groups Measles, Tuberculosis, and Varicella under airborne transmission (under 5 microns) requiring an N95 mask and a negative-pressure room with door closed; droplet precautions cover pertussis, influenza, meningitis and pneumonia.

questions.prompt: A patient bitten on the face by a dog is brought to the Animal Bite Center. Based on the material, which statement about this exposure is correct?
options: A. A face bite carries about a 60% risk of developing rabies
B. A face bite carries the lowest risk at about 10%
C. Rabies from a face bite is rarely fatal once symptoms appear
D. Lower-extremity bites carry the highest risk at 60%
questions.rationale: The source states the risk of developing rabies is 60% for a face bite, 15-40% for upper extremities, and 10% for lower extremities, and that rabies is 100% fatal once it develops.

questions.prompt: A child in the febrile (Day 1-3) phase of dengue has a fever of 40C. Which antipyretic measure is appropriate and which must be AVOIDED per the material?
options: A. Give paracetamol and avoid aspirin and NSAIDs because of bleeding risk
B. Give aspirin and avoid paracetamol because of hepatotoxicity
C. Give ibuprofen and avoid tepid sponge bath
D. Give corticosteroids to suppress the cytokine storm
questions.rationale: Dengue management in the source uses tepid sponge bath and paracetamol every 4-6 hours, and explicitly avoids aspirin and NSAIDs (bleeding risk) as well as corticosteroids (immune suppression, hyperglycemia).

questions.prompt: A nurse caring for a patient with tetanus reviews the drug of choice, metronidazole. Which health teaching is most important?
options: A. Avoid alcoholic beverages because they inhibit drug absorption
B. Take the drug with calcium-rich foods to improve tolerance
C. Expect red-orange discoloration of body secretions
D. Take pyridoxine to prevent peripheral neuritis
questions.rationale: The material lists metronidazole as the drug of choice for tetanus with the nursing reminder to avoid alcoholic beverages, which inhibit drug absorption; the calcium-avoidance reminder applies to the alternative, tetracycline.

questions.prompt: A nurse assesses a child suspected of having measles. Which finding is the pathognomonic sign of this disease?
questions.rationale: The source identifies Koplik's spots as the pathognomonic sign of measles; Forchheimer's spots are seen in German measles/rubella, rose spots in typhoid fever, and risus sardonicus in tetanus.

questions.prompt: When applying the chain of infection, which intervention BEST targets the mode of transmission?
options: A. Hand hygiene and cleaning of high-touch environmental surfaces
B. Vaccinating people to improve host resistance
C. Covering coughs and sneezes with a tissue
D. Keeping surgical wounds covered with a dressing
questions.rationale: The material lists hand hygiene, glove use, cleaning/disinfection of shared equipment and cleaning of high-touch surfaces as ways to eliminate the mode of transmission; vaccination targets the susceptible host, covering coughs targets the portal of exit, and wound dressings protect the portal of entry.

questions.prompt: Under RA 11332 (Mandatory Reporting of Notifiable Diseases), which condition must be reported within 24 hours as a Category I event?
questions.rationale: The source places measles (along with rabies, SARS, COVID-19, neonatal tetanus and others) under Category I requiring reporting within 24 hours, whereas dengue, leptospirosis and typhoid are listed under Category II weekly reporting.

banks.title: Maternal and Child Health Nursing: Obstetric, Pediatric Growth and Development, and Common Pediatric Disorders

questions.prompt: A nurse reviews the menstrual cycle with a client. Which hormone is responsible for triggering ovulation by causing the release of a mature ovum from the ovary?
questions.rationale: Per the material, LH (Luteinizing Hormone) triggers ovulation, the release of a mature ovum, and stimulates the ovary to produce progesterone, while FSH handles maturation of the ovum and GnRH stimulates the pituitary to release FSH and LH.

questions.prompt: A pregnant client at 8 weeks' gestation reports that her husband has been experiencing nausea and fatigue similar to her own symptoms. The nurse documents this as which finding?
questions.rationale: The material defines Couvade syndrome (sympathetic pregnancy) as signs of pregnancy felt by the husband. Ambivalence is mixed emotions on learning of pregnancy, quickening is fetal movement felt by the mother, and Chadwick's sign is bluish discoloration of the vagina.

questions.prompt: During a prenatal class, a nurse explains the first placental hormone produced and the basis for a positive pregnancy test. Which hormone is being described?
questions.rationale: The material states hCG is the first placental hormone, appears in maternal serum as early as 24-48 hours after implantation, prolongs the corpus luteum, and is the basis for pregnancy testing.

questions.prompt: A nurse caring for a laboring woman notes the umbilical cord has prolapsed and is visible at the vaginal opening. Which is the priority nursing action?
options: A. Attempt to reinsert the cord into the vagina
B. Place the woman supine and prepare for immediate ambulation
C. Cover the exposed cord with wet (NSS-moistened) gauze and reposition (e.g., knee-chest or Trendelenburg)
D. Apply firm fundal pressure to deliver quickly
questions.rationale: The material directs that if the cord is exposed, cover it with wet gauze, and for cord compression reposition the mother (Sim's, Trendelenburg, knee-chest, or hands and knees). It explicitly says do not reinsert the cord.

questions.prompt: A woman in the active phase of the first stage of labor asks how dilated she is. Which cervical dilatation range corresponds to the active phase?
questions.rationale: The material specifies the active phase involves cervical dilatation of 4-7 cm; the latent phase is 0-3 cm and the transition phase is 8-10 cm.

questions.prompt: During the fourth stage of labor, the nurse palpates the fundus and finds it soft, relaxed, and boggy. This finding most likely indicates which condition?
questions.rationale: The material states that a fundus that is soft, relaxed, and boggy indicates uterine atony; a fundus deviated to the side suggests a full bladder, and a firm fundus with a steady trickle of blood suggests laceration.

questions.prompt: A client is receiving magnesium sulfate for severe pre-eclampsia. The nurse must withhold the next dose if which assessment finding is present?
options: A. Respiratory rate below 12 breaths per minute
questions.rationale: The material lists magnesium toxicity parameters including respiratory rate <12, and states 'If RR <12/<14 do not give.' A patellar reflex of +2 is normal and urine output of 40 mL/hr is above the toxicity threshold of <30 mL/hr.

questions.prompt: A pregnant woman presents with sudden, painless, bright red vaginal bleeding at about 30 weeks' gestation, and her uterus is soft and non-tender. Which condition is most consistent with these findings?
questions.rationale: The material characterizes placenta previa by painless, bright red bleeding (around 30 weeks) with a soft, non-tender uterus, in contrast to abruptio placenta, which presents with painful, dark/bright red bleeding and a board-like, tender uterus.

questions.prompt: A newborn is assessed at 1 minute of life: heart rate 90, slow irregular respirations with a weak cry, some flexion of extremities, grimace to suction, and a body that is pink with blue extremities. What is this newborn's APGAR score?
questions.rationale: Using the material's APGAR criteria: pulse <100 = 1, weak cry respiration = 1, minimal/some flexion activity = 1, grimace = 1, acrocyanosis appearance = 1, totaling 5 (FAIR), which needs further observation, stimulation, and suctioning.

questions.prompt: According to Erikson's psychosocial stages as presented, the toddler is working to achieve which developmental task?
options: A. Viewing the world as safe and reliable (trust)
B. Achieving a sense of control and free will (autonomy)
C. Beginning development of a conscience (initiative)
D. Emerging confidence in own abilities (industry)
questions.rationale: The material places the toddler in Autonomy vs. Shame and Doubt, with the task of achieving a sense of control and free will (virtue: Will). Trust is the infant stage, initiative is preschool, and industry is school age.

questions.prompt: The mother of a 10-month-old infant asks what play behavior is normal for this age. According to the material, which type of play is characteristic of infancy?
questions.rationale: The material lists solitary play for the infant, parallel play for the toddler, associative/imitation play for the preschooler, and outdoor competitive play for the adolescent.

questions.prompt: A nurse is feeding a newborn with a cleft lip awaiting cheiloplasty. The 'Rule of 10' criteria for scheduling surgical repair include which of the following?
options: A. 10 weeks of age, 10 lbs, 10,000 WBC, and 10 g/dL hemoglobin
B. 10 days of age, 10 oz, and 10 g/dL hemoglobin
C. 10 months of age and 10 kg weight
D. 10 weeks of age and 10 cm head circumference
questions.rationale: The material's Rule of 10 for cheiloplasty (cleft lip repair) lists 10 weeks, 10 lbs, 10,000 WBC, and 10 g/dL hemoglobin, whereas palatoplasty is timed at 18-24 months.

questions.prompt: An infant with tetralogy of Fallot becomes acutely cyanotic and irritable. The nurse observes the child squatting. What is the physiologic purpose of squatting in this child?
options: A. It increases venous return to overload the right ventricle
B. It decreases venous return, reducing cardiac workload and conserving oxygen for vital organs
C. It opens the ductus arteriosus to improve mixing
D. It relieves the machine-like murmur of the defect
questions.rationale: The material explains that in tetralogy of Fallot, squatting decreases venous return, which decreases cardiac workload (cardiac rest) and conserves oxygen in the upper body for the vital organs. The machine-like murmur belongs to patent ductus arteriosus.

questions.prompt: A child is admitted with suspected increased intracranial pressure. Which set of findings represents Cushing's triad as described in the material?
questions.rationale: The material defines Cushing's triad in increased intracranial pressure as hypertension, bradycardia, and bradypnea, along with a widened pulse pressure.

banks.title: Emergency & Critical Care, Cardiology, Oncology, Orthopedics, and Respiratory Nursing

questions.prompt: During triage in a busy emergency department, four patients arrive at once. Using the 3-level urgency system, which patient is classified as Emergent (Level I) and must be seen first?
options: A. A patient in respiratory failure following anaphylaxis
B. A patient with a high fever and acute infection
C. A patient requesting a routine check-up for a chronic condition
D. A patient with a minor laceration to the forearm
questions.rationale: In the 3-level triage system, Level I (Emergent) is reserved for life-threatening ABC problems such as cardiac arrest, severe trauma, acute stroke, respiratory failure, and anaphylaxis. High fever/acute infection is Urgent (II) and chronic conditions, minor injuries, and routine check-ups are Non-urgent (III).

questions.prompt: A nurse is performing the primary survey on an unconscious trauma patient who is breathing spontaneously. According to the material, which airway adjunct is indicated?
options: A. Nasopharyngeal airway, because the patient has facial trauma
B. Oropharyngeal airway, since the patient is unconscious and breathing spontaneously
C. Endotracheal intubation, because ventilation is absent
D. No airway is needed because the patient is breathing
questions.rationale: The oropharyngeal airway (OPA) is indicated for an unconscious patient who is breathing spontaneously; it is contraindicated in conscious or semi-conscious patients because it triggers the gag reflex. Facial trauma is a contraindication to the NPA, and endotracheal intubation is indicated for absent ventilation or persistent hypoxia.

questions.prompt: A nurse is performing CPR alone on an adult in cardiac arrest with no advanced airway in place. What compression-to-ventilation ratio and compression depth should be used?
options: A. 15:2 ratio at a depth of 1.5 inches
B. 30:2 ratio at a depth of 2 inches
C. 5:1 ratio at a depth of 1 inch
D. Continuous compressions only at a depth of 2 inches
questions.rationale: For a single rescuer performing adult BLS, the compression-to-ventilation ratio is 30:2 with a compression depth of 2 inches at a rate of 100-120 bpm, allowing complete chest recoil.

questions.prompt: A patient sustains deep burns. The nurse notes pearly white, leathery skin areas that the patient reports as painless. How should these burns be classified?
options: D. Sunburn with intact nerve endings
questions.rationale: Third-degree (full-thickness) burns extend to the subcutaneous layer and appear pearly white or yellow with damaged nerves, making them painless. First-degree burns are reddish and painful with intact nerves; second-degree burns are moist with blisters and painful.

questions.prompt: A burn patient is in the emergent (resuscitative) phase. Which set of findings is the nurse most likely to assess during this phase?
options: C. Hypocalcemia from scab formation and normal urine output
questions.rationale: In the emergent phase, fluid shifts from the intravascular to the interstitial space (capillary leak), producing hypovolemia (burn shock), hemoconcentration (increased hematocrit), and oliguria. Hypervolemia, hemodilution, and diuresis characterize the later acute phase.

questions.prompt: A patient in distributive shock from a spinal cord injury presents with hypotension. Which vital sign pattern distinguishes neurogenic shock from the other shock states in the material?
options: A. Hypotension with tachycardia and tachypnea
C. Hypotension with bradycardia (no SNS response)
D. Normal blood pressure with bounding pulses
questions.rationale: Neurogenic shock results from loss of sympathetic nervous system response, so unlike hypovolemic, cardiogenic, septic, and anaphylactic shock (which present with hypotension plus tachycardia/tachypnea), neurogenic shock presents with hypotension and bradycardia.

questions.prompt: A conscious adult is clutching the throat, unable to cough, speak, or breathe, with stridor and cyanosis. What is the appropriate immediate intervention?
options: A. Encourage the patient to cough forcefully
C. Begin chest compressions and a blind finger sweep
questions.rationale: Inability to cough, speak, or breathe with clutching of the neck, cyanosis, and stridor indicates complete airway obstruction in a conscious adult; the abdominal thrust (Heimlich maneuver) is indicated. Forceful coughing is only appropriate for a partial obstruction where the patient can still cough.

questions.prompt: A patient is suspected of having a myocardial infarction. According to the material, which cardiac marker is the most important, reliable, and sensitive blood test and remains elevated for up to two weeks?
questions.rationale: Troponin I is described as the most important, reliable, and sensitive blood test for MI and lasts for about two weeks. Myoglobin is the first to elevate (within 2 hours) but is nonspecific, and CK-MB is the most specific enzyme but does not persist as long.

questions.prompt: A patient with heart failure develops acute pulmonary edema. Which medication is identified as the drug of choice, and how is it given?
options: C. Norepinephrine titrated to a MAP greater than 65 mmHg
questions.rationale: For pulmonary edema in heart failure, the material lists furosemide 40 mg IV STAT as the drug of choice, along with high Fowler's positioning, oxygen, an IV line, and monitoring of intake and output. Norepinephrine and colloids are used in shock, not as the first-line treatment here.

questions.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient receiving a sealed internal radiation implant (brachytherapy). Which action follows the safety principles described in the material?
options: A. Spend extended time at the bedside to provide reassurance
B. Pick up a dislodged implant with the gloved hand and discard it
C. Maintain distance of 6 feet, limit time to about 30 minutes per shift, and use a lead shield
D. Encourage pregnant and pediatric visitors to stay with the patient
questions.rationale: Sealed internal radiation safety follows the Distance-Time-Shield principles: stay about 6 feet away, limit care to roughly 30 minutes per shift while clustering activities, and use a lead shield with a dosimeter badge. A dislodged implant is picked up with long-handled forceps and placed in a lead-lined container, not the hand, and elderly, pediatric, pregnant, and immunocompromised visitors are avoided.

questions.prompt: A nurse reviews warning signs of cancer with a patient. According to the ABCDE assessment tool for melanoma, which mole characteristic is a concerning finding?
options: A. Symmetric shape with smooth, regular borders
B. Asymmetry, irregular borders, and a diameter greater than 5 mm
C. Uniform single color and a diameter of 2 mm
D. A stable lesion that has not changed over years
questions.rationale: The ABCDE tool flags Asymmetry, irregular Borders, Color variation, Diameter (normally less than 5 mm), and Evolving lesions as warning signs of melanoma. Symmetric, uniformly colored, small, and stable lesions are reassuring.

questions.prompt: A patient with a long-bone fracture develops sudden dyspnea, confusion, and a petechial rash over the upper body 48 hours after injury. Which complication does this classic triad indicate?
questions.rationale: Fat embolism syndrome occurs within 24-72 hours of injury and is identified by the classic triad of hypoxemia, neurologic changes, and a petechial rash (upper body, conjunctiva, oral mucosa). Compartment syndrome presents with the 6 P's, and DVT presents with unilateral calf findings.

questions.prompt: A nurse assesses a patient in a cast for compartment syndrome. Which finding is the priority concern, and which sign is described as a late finding?
options: A. Severe pain unrelieved by opioids is the priority concern; pulselessness is a late sign
B. Pulselessness is the earliest reliable sign; pain appears last
C. Warmth and redness are the priority; paralysis appears first
D. Tingling is benign and requires no intervention
questions.rationale: Compartment syndrome assessment uses the 6 P's; severe pain that is unrelieved by opioids and disproportionate is an early hallmark, whereas pulselessness is described as a late sign. Neurologic damage may become irreversible if untreated within 4-12 hours, making early recognition critical.

questions.prompt: A nurse interprets an arterial blood gas showing a low pH with an elevated PCO2. Using the steps described, which acid-base imbalance does this represent?
questions.rationale: PCO2 is the respiratory indicator and moves opposite to pH ("Respiratory Opposite"); a low pH with a high PCO2 indicates respiratory acidosis, which occurs with hypoventilation. The HCO3 (metabolic indicator, "Metabolic Equal") would be the abnormal value in metabolic disorders.

banks.title: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Renal/Urinary, Endocrine, Immunology, Fluids & Electrolytes, and Gastrointestinal

questions.prompt: A client with chronic kidney disease has a GFR of 12 mL/min/1.73 m2. Which stage of chronic renal failure does this represent?
options: A. Stage 1 (kidney damage with normal GFR)
D. Stage 5 / CKD V (end-stage renal disease)
questions.rationale: Per the staging in the material, a GFR of 15 mL/min/1.73 m2 or lower defines Stage 5 / CKD V, which is kidney failure (end-stage renal disease). A GFR of 12 is below 15, so it is Stage 5.

questions.prompt: A nurse is preparing to administer IV potassium to a client with a serum potassium of 2.9 mEq/L. Which action is correct?
options: A. Administer the potassium by rapid IV push to correct the deficit quickly
B. Dilute the potassium in at least 100 mL of fluid and infuse via pump while monitoring the ECG
C. Give the potassium undiluted intramuscularly
D. Withhold potassium because the level is within normal limits
questions.rationale: The material states IV potassium must NEVER be given IV push or IM; it should always be diluted in at least 100 mL of fluid, infused via an infusion pump, with ECG monitoring during the infusion. A level of 2.9 is below the normal 3.5 mEq/L.

questions.prompt: A client is admitted with hyperkalemia (serum potassium 6.8 mEq/L). Which ECG change is most consistent with this electrolyte imbalance?
questions.rationale: The material lists tall, tented T waves (along with prolonged PR/QRS and absent P waves) as ECG findings of hyperkalemia. Prominent U waves and flattened T waves are seen in hypokalemia, and a shortened QT interval is associated with hypercalcemia.

questions.prompt: A client with SIADH is being evaluated. Which set of findings would the nurse expect?
options: A. Polyuria with dilute urine, hypernatremia, and weight loss
B. Fluid volume excess, dilutional hyponatremia, and elevated urine specific gravity
C. Excessive thirst, low urine specific gravity, and dehydration
D. Decreased ADH level with high serum osmolality
questions.rationale: The material describes SIADH as excessive ADH causing fluid volume excess, weight gain, oliguria with elevated urine specific gravity (>1.030), and dilutional hyponatremia. Polyuria, dilute urine, hypernatremia, and dehydration describe diabetes insipidus instead.

questions.prompt: A nurse is assessing a client with Addison's disease. Which finding is the hallmark sign of this disorder?
options: A. Buffalo hump and moon-face appearance
D. Central obesity with purple striae
questions.rationale: The material identifies bronze skin discoloration (dark pigmentation) as the hallmark of Addison's disease, along with hypotension, low sodium, high potassium, and low blood glucose. The buffalo hump, moon face, hypertension, hypokalemia, and purple striae are features of Cushing's disease.

questions.prompt: Following a subtotal thyroidectomy, which postoperative assessment is the nurse's number-one priority?
options: A. Monitoring for airway obstruction and stridor
D. Checking for bronze skin pigmentation
questions.rationale: The material lists AIRWAY as the #1 postoperative priority after thyroidectomy, with stridor signaling large-airway obstruction; a tracheostomy set, oxygen, and suction are kept at the bedside.

questions.prompt: A client taking methimazole (Tapazole) for hyperthyroidism develops a sore throat, fever, and mouth ulcers. What is the most appropriate nursing instruction?
options: A. Continue the medication and take it with food to reduce nausea
B. Double the next dose to control symptoms more quickly
C. Stop the medication and notify the physician immediately for hematologic studies
D. Reassure the client that these are expected, harmless side effects
questions.rationale: The material states agranulocytosis is the most toxic side effect of antithyroid drugs; with any sign of infection (especially sore throat/pharyngitis), myalgia, fever, or mouth ulcers, the client should stop the medication, notify the physician immediately, and undergo hematologic studies.

questions.prompt: A client with type 1 diabetes presents with a blood glucose of 480 mg/dL, fruity (acetone) breath, and deep rapid respirations. These deep rapid respirations are best described as:
questions.rationale: The material describes the rapid, deep breathing of diabetic ketoacidosis as Kussmaul's respiration, occurring with hyperglycemia, acetone breath, and acidosis.

questions.prompt: A nurse is reviewing insulin onset times. Which insulin is classified as rapid-acting?
questions.rationale: The material classifies lispro (Humalog), aspart, and glulisine as rapid-acting insulins (onset 15-30 minutes). Regular is short-acting, NPH is intermediate-acting, and glargine is long-acting.

questions.prompt: A client develops anaphylaxis after a bee sting. Which type of hypersensitivity reaction does this represent?
options: A. Type I (immediate/anaphylactic), mediated by IgE
B. Type II (cytotoxic), mediated by IgG or IgM
D. Type IV (delayed/cell-mediated), mediated by T lymphocytes
questions.rationale: The material classifies anaphylaxis as a Type I (immediate/anaphylactic) hypersensitivity reaction mediated by IgE antibodies, with onset within minutes. Type II involves cell destruction, Type III involves immune complexes, and Type IV is delayed and T-cell mediated.

questions.prompt: A client with a calcium oxalate (acidic) renal stone asks about diet. Which recommendation is correct based on the material?
options: A. Increase intake of spinach, tea, and chocolate
B. Restrict fluids to less than 1 liter per day
C. Follow an alkaline-ash diet and force fluids to about 3 L/day
D. Increase organ meats and sardines
questions.rationale: The material directs an alkaline-ash diet for acidic stones and forcing fluids to about 3 L/day to help pass the stone. Spinach, tea, and chocolate are oxalate sources to avoid, and organ meats/sardines are high-purine foods linked to uric acid stones.

questions.prompt: A nurse caring for a client on peritoneal dialysis notes that the dialysate drainage returns cloudy. What does this finding most likely indicate?
options: A. A normal finding for all exchanges
D. Bleeding, which is normal at first
questions.rationale: The material states the normal drainage color is colorless; cloudy drainage indicates infection/peritonitis. Yellowish suggests a punctured bladder, and bloody drainage is normal only in the first few exchanges.

questions.prompt: A client with suspected acute appendicitis reports severe right lower quadrant pain. Prior to surgical evaluation, which intervention is appropriate?
options: A. Apply a hot compress to the abdomen to relieve pain
B. Administer analgesics liberally to keep the client comfortable
C. Keep the client NPO and on bed rest, applying a cold compress
D. Encourage ambulation and a high-fiber meal
questions.rationale: The material advises decreasing GI activity (NPO, bed rest) and using a cold compress, while avoiding analgesics in suspected appendicitis (they can mask pain or precipitate rupture) and avoiding hot compresses, which can promote rupture.

questions.prompt: A client with peptic ulcer disease is prescribed sucralfate, a cytoprotective agent. When should this medication be administered?
options: C. Only at bedtime with milk
D. At the same time as an antacid
questions.rationale: The material states cytoprotective agents such as sucralfate, which form a protective barrier over the ulcer, are given before meals. Antacids, by contrast, are timed 1-2 hours after meals.

banks.title: Psychiatric and Mental Health Nursing, Psychopharmacology, Professional Adjustment, Nursing Jurisprudence and Ethics, Leadership and Management, and Nursing Research

questions.prompt: A client experiencing auditory hallucinations tells the nurse, "The voices are telling me to hurt myself." Which initial nursing response is most therapeutic?
options: A. "There are no voices. You are safe here in the hospital."
B. "It must be frightening that you are hearing those voices."
C. "You should just ignore the voices and they will go away."
D. "Why do you think the voices want you to hurt yourself?"
questions.rationale: Per the material's management of hallucinations, the nurse first recognizes/acknowledges the experience with a statement such as "It must be frightening that you are hearing those voices," which validates the client's feelings before assessing the content. Flatly denying reality, dismissing, or asking "why" are not the recommended initial responses.

questions.prompt: A client states, "I have nothing to live for. I wish I was dead." The nurse replies, "Everybody gets down in the dumps; I've felt that way myself." This response is an example of which non-therapeutic technique?
questions.rationale: The source identifies equating a client's intense feelings to "everybody" or to the nurse's own feelings as belittling feelings expressed, which implies the discomfort is mild or unimportant. Presenting reality, reflecting, and suggesting collaboration are listed as therapeutic techniques.

questions.prompt: A nurse caring for a client taking a first-generation antipsychotic notes a temperature of 41°C, severe muscle rigidity, and unstable blood pressure. Which condition does the nurse suspect, and what is the priority action?
options: A. Tardive dyskinesia; document and continue the medication
B. Acute dystonia; administer benztropine and continue the dose
C. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome; stop the medication and notify the physician
D. Akathisia; encourage the client to walk to relieve restlessness
questions.rationale: The material describes neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) as a potentially fatal reaction marked by hyperthermia (up to 41°C), muscle spasms/rigidity, and hypertensive crisis, with the nursing action being to stop the medication and notify the MD. Tardive dyskinesia, dystonia, and akathisia present differently.

questions.prompt: A client receiving lithium reports increasing fine hand tremors. The nurse knows that the therapeutic serum lithium level is which of the following?
questions.rationale: The source lists the therapeutic lithium range as 0.6–1.2 mEq/L, with tremors as an early sign and adequate salt/hydration as essential. The other ranges are not the stated therapeutic lithium level.

questions.prompt: A client is admitted with anorexia nervosa. Which assessment finding is most consistent with this diagnosis?
options: A. Average body weight with calluses on the knuckles (Russell's sign)
B. Enlarged parotid glands and frequent dental caries
C. Body weight 15% or more below ideal body weight with intense fear of gaining weight
D. Binge eating with no compensatory purging or exercise
questions.rationale: The material characterizes anorexia nervosa by restriction of intake, underweight (15% or less than IBW), and intense fear of gaining weight. Russell's sign, enlarged parotid glands, and dental caries are listed under bulimia nervosa, and binge eating without compensation describes binge eating disorder.

questions.prompt: A client with a known alcohol use disorder is prescribed disulfiram (Antabuse). Which instruction is most important for the nurse to include in discharge teaching?
options: A. "Take vitamin B complex foods such as nuts and pork to prevent deficiency."
B. "Avoid products containing alcohol such as mouthwash, aftershave, and cologne."
C. "Expect mild drowsiness, which is a normal effect of this medication."
D. "You may resume social drinking after two weeks of therapy."
questions.rationale: The source states that clients on disulfiram must avoid alcohol-containing products such as mouthwash, aftershave lotion, cologne, vinegar, and isopropyl alcohol, because exposure triggers a disulfiram reaction (intense headache, nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal cramps). Resuming drinking is contraindicated.

questions.prompt: Using Freud's defense mechanisms, a person who is angry at the boss goes home and yells at the spouse. Which defense mechanism is being used?
questions.rationale: The material defines displacement as the ventilation of intense feelings toward persons less threatening than the one who aroused those feelings, giving the example of a person mad at the boss yelling at his or her spouse. The other mechanisms have different definitions and examples.

questions.prompt: According to Erikson's psychosocial stages, an 8-year-old child who takes pleasure in accomplishments and is developing confidence in his abilities is working through which stage?
questions.rationale: The source places Industry vs. Inferiority in the school-age period (6–12 years), with emerging confidence in one's own abilities and taking pleasure in accomplishments. Trust, Initiative, and Identity stages correspond to other age ranges.

questions.prompt: A client experiencing severe anxiety is pacing, has tachycardia and diaphoresis, and cannot be redirected to a task. Which nursing approach is most appropriate?
options: A. Do nothing, as this level of anxiety promotes learning
B. Use open-ended questions and encourage independent problem solving
C. Use direct questions, give IM medication as ordered, and stay to ensure safety
D. Leave the client alone in a quiet room without any staff present
questions.rationale: The material's management of severe anxiety specifies directives/direct questions, IM medications, and staying with the client to ensure safety, because the person cannot focus or be redirected to a task. "Do nothing" applies to mild anxiety, and problem solving with assistance applies to moderate anxiety.

questions.prompt: A nurse intentionally performs an unconsented physical procedure on a competent client who refused it. Which tort has the nurse most directly committed?
questions.rationale: The material defines battery as the intentional, unconsented physical touching of another person. Assault is the imminent threat of harmful contact (a verbal threat), false imprisonment is unjustifiable detention, and defamation is character assassination.

questions.prompt: Under RA 9173 (the Philippine Nursing Act of 2002), within what period may a nurse file an appeal with the PRC after receiving a suspension or revocation order?
questions.rationale: The source states that an appeal must be filed with the Professional Regulatory Commission (PRC) within a period of 30 days after the suspension or revocation order has been received (the reglementary period).

questions.prompt: A nurse manager assigns a particular nursing function—such as taking vital signs—to each worker so that one staff member performs that single task for all patients. This pattern of care is best described as which nursing modality?
questions.rationale: The material describes functional nursing as a task-oriented modality in which a particular nursing function is assigned to each worker; its disadvantages include fragmentation of care and the patient being unable to identify their real nurse. Primary, team, and case methods organize care differently.

questions.prompt: In the research process, a study that collects data on an outcome occurring in the present and then links it retrospectively to determinants occurring in the past is using which time-frame design?
questions.rationale: The source defines a retrospective design as one that involves collecting data on an outcome occurring in the present and then linking it retrospectively to antecedents or determinants occurring in the past. Prospective moves from cause to effect, cross-sectional collects data once, and longitudinal collects data at more than one point over time.

questions.prompt: A nutritional disorder shows a child with normal carbohydrate intake but low protein, thin extremities, moon face, ascites, and thin sparse hair. Identify the condition.
questions.rationale: The module describes Kwashiorkor as normal carbs with low protein, producing fluid shifting (moon face, ascites) and thin sparse hair. Marasmus, by contrast, is low in both carbs and protein with a skin-and-bones, wrinkled appearance.

questions.prompt: Which Republic Act (2011) mandates basic immunization for children below 5 years old?
questions.rationale: RA 10152 (2011) provides for mandatory immunization of children under 5. (RA 11036 is the Mental Health Law — a common distractor.)

questions.prompt: The Pentavalent (5-in-1) vaccine protects against five diseases. Enumerate all five.
questions.rationale: Per the module, the Pentavalent (5-in-1) vaccine covers Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tuberculosis, Hepatitis B, and HiB.

questions.prompt: Name THREE vaccines listed as most sensitive to heat (stored in the freezer at -15°C to -25°C).
questions.rationale: The module lists Varicella, OPV, and MMR as the freezer-stored, most heat-sensitive vaccines.

questions.prompt: Match each level of prevention to its correct activity.

pairs.right: Health education and immunization while the patient is healthy
Limiting disability and restoring functional capability

questions.rationale: Primary = health promotion/illness prevention (immunization); Secondary = early detection and prompt treatment; Tertiary = rehabilitation, limiting disability and restoring function.

questions.prompt: Match each community-health concept to its correct goal or definition.
questions.rationale: PHC aims for self-reliance in health; COPAR aims for community health development; the family is the basic unit of service/care.
